History is my passion, with a strong focus on genealogy and family history. I've done extensive research on my family so inevitably I've collected a few interesting ones. I thought it might be fun, interesting, and a nice escape from the election to share. I hope you have some you will share too.

Here's one from my paternal line: Next month, will be the anniversary of the 154th anniversary of the Sioux Uprising. One of my ancestors was employed as a clerk for the Upper Agency in Yellow Medicine, MN. He resided at there with his wife and two small children. Unlike Maj. Galbraith, who was in charge of the Agency and a very hated man by the Sioux, my ancestor was quite well liked. He was friendly with John Otherday, a Red Bird who lived there too. On the night when the Sioux were raiding the Lower Agency, John Otherday went to the Upper Agency to warn the settlers of what was going on down river. He arranged to help them all, including women and children, escape by a wagon caravan in the middle of the night. Where it not for the heroic actions of John Otherday, my ancestors and almost 60 other settlers on the Agency would have been wiped out by the Sioux.

If you're interested in reading about it, there is more in this book - A History of the Great Massacre by the Sioux Indians, in Minnesota, by Charles S. Bryant - start at the paragraph that says 'During all the fatal 18th of August..."

Thanks John Otherday! I wouldn't be here without you.
